pr.title: Add cache for IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin

raw_findings.body: The login caches keep the IDP's internal id. After the organization is re-enabled (an org update never triggers IDP login-cache invalidation), getForLogin still returns the IDP; in the hideOnLogin case its isEnabled() is true, so the login page shows an IDP that was configured to be hidden, until some unrelated invalidation occurs.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cache invalidation is silently skipped for a state transition that changes the DB-level query result, so getForLogin serves stale entries and hidden/disabled IDPs can reappear on the login page.
raw_findings.impact: The login caches keep the IDP's internal id. After the organization is re-enabled (an org update never triggers IDP login-cache invalidation), getForLogin still returns the IDP; in the hideOnLogin case its isEnabled() is true, so the login page shows an IDP that was configured to be hidden, until some unrelated invalidation occurs.
raw_findings.root_cause: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate tests getLoginPredicate() on the org-aware wrapped `original` model, whose isEnabled() depends on the organization's state, while the cached set was built from a DB query that only checks the IDP's own ENABLED column.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the invalidation predicates against the raw delegate model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())) instead of the org-aware wrapped model returned by getById(), so the qualification test matches the DB-level query used to populate the login cache.
raw_findings.title: Login-cache invalidation skipped when updating an IDP whose organization is disabled, leaving stale getForLogin results
raw_findings.trigger: An IDP is linked to a currently disabled organization while it is DB-enabled, public, and present in a cached getForLogin result set; an admin then updates the IDP to disqualify it from login (e.g. sets hideOnLogin=true or enabled=false). `original` comes from getById(), which returns the org-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false because the org is disabled, so getLoginPredicate().test(original) is false, getLoginPredicate().test(updated) is also false, and the method returns without invalidating, even though the delegate query that populated the cache (which filters only on the DB ENABLED column) had included this IDP.

raw_findings.body: An extra database round-trip on every IDP removal even when the model is available from `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)`, a small but avoidable regression on a code path that previously avoided the query.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary DB query per removal, partially defeating the purpose of the cache layer on this path.
raw_findings.impact: An extra database round-trip on every IDP removal even when the model is available from `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)`, a small but avoidable regression on a code path that previously avoided the query.
raw_findings.root_cause: The delegate lookup was hoisted above the cache-hit branch to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation, discarding the previously used cached model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In the non-invalid branch, reuse `cached.getIdentityProvider()` for the login invalidation check and fall back to `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` only when no cached entry exists or the key is invalid.
raw_findings.title: remove() performs an unconditional delegate getByAlias DB lookup even when the IDP is already cached
raw_findings.trigger: Removing an IDP whose alias entry is present in the realm cache and not invalidated; before this patch the delegate lookup only happened on the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch, now it runs on every removal.

raw_findings.body: None of the 20 created identity providers are removed during cleanup (the remove call targets a nonexistent IDP and 404s), so realm state leaks into subsequently executed tests in this class/realm, causing order-dependent failures.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test isolation is broken: created fixtures persist beyond the test while cleanup silently fails against a nonexistent resource.
raw_findings.impact: None of the 20 created identity providers are removed during cleanup (the remove call targets a nonexistent IDP and 404s), so realm state leaks into subsequently executed tests in this class/realm, causing order-dependent failures.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of a placeholder alias string "alias" into the cleanup registration instead of the alias actually assigned to the representation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Capture the alias in a variable and register `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove);` (using an effectively-final copy of the alias).
raw_findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of nonexistent alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias (creation loop)
raw_findings.trigger: Test teardown after testCacheIDPForLogin runs: the cleanup task targets a fixed literal alias "alias" rather than "idp-alias-" + i for each of the 20 created IDPs.

raw_findings.body: The "idp-alias-20" provider (which by the end of the test is org-linked and login-visible) is never removed, leaking into other tests running against the same realm and making them order-dependent.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cleanup targets a nonexistent IDP, leaving the created fixture in the realm after the test completes.
raw_findings.impact: The "idp-alias-20" provider (which by the end of the test is org-linked and login-visible) is never removed, leaking into other tests running against the same realm and making them order-dependent.
raw_findings.root_cause: Placeholder alias "alias" used in the cleanup registration instead of the alias set on the representation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Register the cleanup with the real alias: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove);`.
raw_findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of nonexistent alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-20"
raw_findings.trigger: Test teardown after testCacheIDPForLogin: the cleanup for the IDP created with alias "idp-alias-20" instead references the literal alias "alias".

raw_findings.body: If the invalidation in create()/remove() for qualifying IDPs regresses (e.g. is dropped or the predicate is wrong for the raw delegate model), the test suite would still pass while login pages serve stale IDP lists after adding or deleting a broker.
raw_findings.evidence: // 1- add/remove IDPs that are not available for login - none of these operations should invalidate the login caches.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A regression in registerIDPLoginInvalidation's invalidating path on create/remove would go undetected by the suite.
raw_findings.impact: If the invalidation in create()/remove() for qualifying IDPs regresses (e.g. is dropped or the predicate is wrong for the raw delegate model), the test suite would still pass while login pages serve stale IDP lists after adding or deleting a broker.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test verifies the negative (no-invalidation) cases for create/remove but never the positive invalidation cases for those two operations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a step that creates a login-qualifying IDP (enabled, not hidden, not link-only) and another that removes one of the existing login-qualifying IDPs, asserting after each that all cacheKeyForLogin entries were invalidated and that repopulated counts reflect the change.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for login-cache invalidation on create/remove of a login-qualifying IDP
raw_findings.trigger: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates a hideOnLogin=true IDP and removes a disabled IDP in step 1, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation() is only ever exercised on its no-op branch for create() and remove(); the invalidating branch is only exercised indirectly via update().

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that org-aware wrapper causes stale cache is speculative. The scenario requires multiple state transitions not clearly triggered by this patch.
